A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MOSAIC research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v4 reports original experiments on 50 synthetic advertising queries across 25 seeds, including advertiser rewards, revenue, user-usefulness proxies, and payment-offset analyses.

after.justification: v5 retains those original experiments and adds results for more advertisers, computational timing, advertiser mentions, and FLAN-T5-large.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains candidate generation, importance-weighted softmax selection, and the same objective. Rochet payments and the advertiser-specific offset are also retained. Revised notation and computational explanations do not establish a changed mechanism.

E1.justification: Appendix C.5 extends auction input conditions from two advertisers to five and ten advertisers per query. This is a limited extension to denser auctions using the same 50 user queries; the additional language model and newly printed prompts do not introduce another query domain or task.

E2.justification: The context-aware versus reference-generated MOSAIC comparisons, reference-sampling benchmarks, and payment-offset comparisons are retained. Dütting and VCG receive additional discussion but are not newly evaluated auction baselines.

E3.justification: New protocols include five- and ten-advertiser experiments with tau = n/2, FLAN-T5-large evaluations, and single-A100 timing measurements over 50 instances with up to 30 candidate replies. Appendix C.7 adds the fraction of advertisers mentioned as a measurement. The original two-advertiser Llama-2 protocol remains unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices C.5–C.8 add substantial analyses of advertiser-count scaling, computational costs and their components, advertiser mentions as candidate count increases, and robustness across language models. The original payment-offset ablations and user-usefulness analysis remain.

E5.justification: v5 specifies 20 seeds for the new larger-auction experiments and 10 seeds for FLAN-T5-large, yielding 1,000 and 500 instances respectively. The original 25-seed study is retained. New timing and larger-auction plots report 95% confidence intervals, continuing the existing uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Original Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–2 retain their results. Figures 8–16 add larger-auction and FLAN outcomes, declining advertiser-mention fractions, and timing measurements: generating 10 and 20 replies takes 30.5 and 60.5 seconds versus 12.0 seconds for one. FLAN results also show declining reference-model log probability as candidate count increases. These are new-condition findings, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: v4 already contains asymptotic convergence proofs and the importance-sampling variance derivation. v5 adds the Chebyshev-based sample-complexity result in Lemma A.3 and a total-variation convergence bound with proof in Theorem A.4, assuming finite sequence support and bounded importance weights. Merely restating the existing variance as Lemmas 4.2/A.2 is not a new result.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution overview, and conclusion retain the central claims of truthful aggregation, convergence without fine-tuning or weight access, contextual generation benefits, and welfare-aligned payments. The added evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v5 adds discussion of tau calibration relative to reserve prices, platform-controlled output constraints, and why the objective can discourage excessive advertiser mentions. It interprets the new model results and distinguishes measured single-GPU timings from projected parallelization benefits. Existing individual-rationality and free-riding discussions remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix D/Table 3 discloses all 50 main-study queries and their first two advertisers and descriptions, whereas v4 supplies templates and illustrative examples. Appendix C.6 adds runtime-component and single-GPU execution details. Additional advertiser descriptions are referred to a code supplement; Appendix C.1 retains its promise of public code and data release.

R1.justification: v5 adds Bergemann et al. and discusses their generalization involving private information and broader distance functions. It also adds Chung et al. for FLAN-T5-large and expands computational positioning against Dütting. The Dütting 2023-to-2024 citation change identifies the same work's publication, not a new cited method.

P1.justification: v5 clarifies true versus reported rewards and optimal versus induced policies, rewrites the practical-computation discussion, and expands importance-sampling explanations and appendix organization. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v5 adds Figures 8–16, including the ten-panel advertiser-count comparison, and the extensive prompt table in Appendix D. Existing displays are retained with some relocation. Figure 3's incorrect revenue caption is corrected, although new Figure 14 labels utility gain as value gain in its caption.

improvement.justification: v4's practical evidence was limited to one language model and two advertisers, without measured runtime. v5 substantially strengthens that evidence through scaling, model, and timing studies, while publishing the main experimental inputs and adding finite-sample analysis. Important qualifications remain: evaluation is synthetic and proxy-based, the five-query cost comparison emphasizes generation time, and parallel latency gains are projected. These limits do not outweigh the substantial gains in evidence and reproducibility.
